findings.answer: The reported diagnostics support bounded mechanical checks, but concrete engineering gaps remain. (1) Restart: attempt() writes result.json before receipt.json. A crash between those writes leaves task_rows() unable to read the receipt; run() calls verify(), which calls task_rows(), before attempt() can repair the missing receipt. Duplicate issue IDs similarly pass reserve()'s initial checks but fail verification after persistence. (3) Guard: applicability is evaluated without ownership=True. A known applicability judgment declaring depends_on_ownership=True can therefore bypass ownership-inventory checks, even though scope/body judgments enforce them. This is a dependency-enforcement gap unless ownership-dependent applicability is explicitly outside the supported contract. (4) Reporting: current_review.prepare() can persist APPROVED_BY_USER authorization, yet summary() still labels every passing package PREPARED_AWAITING_NUMERICAL_APPROVAL; it does not inspect authorization. This misreports preparation state, although actual dispatch authorization depends on omitted runtime code. Current results report 183 passing tests, 16 qualified conditional programs, 384 native/Java probes and 960 synthetic guard checks across 20 programs, with zero target cases and zero substantive repair acceptances.
